title: Consummation and Final Mysteries
summary: The final teachings of consummation. T94 describes the five garments of the Divine Human and the Pentecostal feast in which the Call and Answer become the soul's living food. T95 names the hidden powers in the senses sorted daily. T96 distinguishes the visible and hidden registers of understanding. T97 argues that if even one of the five aspects of the natural were missing, the whole could not stand — and names the five things the Lord makes known. T98 describes how the Lord's truth comes forth through the open gates of the rational's discrete degrees. T99 expounds the three icons in the righteous man — pneumatic, psychic, somatic — and the daily soul-cycle. T100 narrates the First Man's prayer in distress and the Father's threefold sending in answer. T101 distinguishes pruning of surface growths from cutting of structural members. T102 describes mystical seeing during sickness when the soul is briefly loosed. T103 restates the foundation: two substances from the beginning, the beautiful and the bitter, life and death — separating the beautiful forth from the darkness. T104 names the Yes and the Amen as the Calling and the Hearing — the soul's answering that aids regeneration.
organizing_principle: The final mysteries of consummation: T94 opens with the Pentecostal completion; T95-T96 expound hidden things made manifest in the senses and eye; T97-T98 expound the five-fold cosmos held by the Lord and his light passing through the gates; T99-T100 unfold the three icons of the regenerated and the prayer that established them; T101-T102 give discrimination between deep and surface as the soul's final orientation; T103 brackets the corpus by restating the foundational dualism (Two Substances) as a coda after the long journey; T104's closing fragment names the Yes and the Amen as the Call and Hearing that carry the whole work upward.
